blockers.what: send() and launch() return a Promise but refuse a bad deadline by throwing synchronously. A consumer that writes transport.send(...).catch(...) does not catch it (probe B: 'TypeError thrown synchronously past .catch'). SendOptions documents this, but CdpTransport.send, the contract consumers code against, says only that every rejection is a CdpError (packages/cdp-pipe/src/pipe.ts:249 (send), :230 (launch), :100-104 (CdpTransport doc), found by the `unit` tier)

The diff validates two of the unit's three deadlines but not close(graceMs). With close(NaN), until() never times out: deadline - now is NaN, `left <= 0` is never true, and setTimeout(NaN) is 1 ms. A browser that ignores Browser.close then hangs close() forever, which breaks its 'never hangs' promise. Infinity behaves the same, and negative values or 0 shrink every grace to one poll. This predates the diff (f025a57 had the same until()), but the diff added checkTimeout right beside it (packages/cdp-pipe/src/pipe.ts:303-336 (close/shutdown), :428-436 (until), found by the `unit` tier)

A read error on the browser's stderr alone makes the whole CDP channel unusable: 500 ms later every send is refused as closed, while fd 3 and fd 4 and the browser are healthy and no onExit fires (probe C: 'after stderr EIO send -> closed'). The brief asks for exactly this (test 1), so it is not a defect. The cost is that a consumer has to treat 'closed' as 'call close() and relaunch', because the pipe will never recover on its own (packages/cdp-pipe/src/pipe.ts:188, found by the `unit` tier)

Whether a crash reports as exited or closed is decided by wall clock: lost() gives the process exit 500 ms to follow the pipe end (EXIT_AFTER_PIPE_MS, measured as 'the same millisecond' on the fake). If the event loop stalls more than 500 ms between the pipe 'end' and SIGCHLD, a crash reports as closed, and three tests assert exited on that path (packages/cdp-pipe/src/pipe.ts:141, :365-369, found by the `unit` tier)

send() and CdpPipe.launch() are typed Promise-returning but throw TypeError synchronously for a timeoutMs/requestTimeoutMs outside whole 1..2^31-1 ms. A consumer that writes transport.send(...).catch(toRefusal) gets an uncaught throw, and one that awaits gets a TypeError with no kind, which the planned kind mapping cannot place. The CdpTransport doc says every rejection of send() is a CdpError, so fakes in N-010/N-011 tests will never produce it. A per-call deadline computed from a remaining budget (deadline - Date.now(), which can be 0, negative or fractional) hits this path (N-011 refusal mapping, docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-27-bridge-b1.md:423 (Test 23), and N-010 AgentWindows callers of send/launch (plan :367); source pipe.ts:417-418, pipe.ts:396, asserted sync at pipe.test.ts:315,319-321, found by the `seam` tier)

CdpErrorKind has a fifth kind, launch, from CdpPipe.launch (errors.ts:85, pipe.ts:404-406), and ExitInfo carries requested. The plan's N-022 Produces line still lists four kinds and onExit {code, signal}, and N-011 Test 23 maps only exited/closed/cdp/timeout. A Chrome that cannot start reaches the daemon as kind launch with no planned refusal; an if/else mapper would send it to internal rather than browser_offline (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-27-bridge-b1.md:423 (N-011 Test 23) and :137 (N-022 Produces read by N-010/N-011 packets); packets/N-011.json acceptance, found by the `seam` tier)

N-010 Test 8 is written against EXIT_AFTER_PIPE_MS, but the constant is module-private (pipe.ts:309, not exported from index.ts), so the test must copy 500 ms and drifts silently if it changes. Related timing contract: on a broken pipe with the browser alive, waiting requests are rejected closed only after 500 ms; a request whose own timeoutMs is under 500 ms gets kind timeout (-> internal) instead of closed (-> browser_offline) (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-27-bridge-b1.md:378 (N-010 Test 8) and :423 (N-011 Test 23); source pipe.ts:309,515-519, found by the `seam` tier)

docs/README.md says every refusal is a CdpError, with TypeError named only for a bad deadline, and the CdpTransport doc comment says every rejection of send() is a CdpError. params that JSON.stringify cannot serialise (a cycle, a BigInt) make send() reject with a plain TypeError (the throw happens inside the promise executor at the write), and the waiting entry stays until its timer. No caller can reach this from an agent's JSON request today, so the claim is false only for a programming error (docs/README.md:106; packages/cdp-pipe/src/pipe.ts:100, 251, 273, 278, found by the `product` tier)

the README row says consumers depend on CdpTransport and that close reports a group it could not end (onCloseIncomplete), but that report reaches only whoever passed LaunchOptions: CdpTransport has no such member and close() resolves void either way. The product promises that rest on it (design §2.2 close verb: 'окно и процессы задачи закрыты'; §3 row: on close the agent-window processes end, SIGTERM then SIGKILL to the group; SCN-048: a removal that fails is 'recorded as failed, never as freed') hold only if K3 wires onCloseIncomplete at launch into the task record. A K3 or K4 written against the interface alone would answer close as success with a process alive. The §3 row also now states unconditionally what cdp-pipe documents as conditional (docs/README.md:106; packages/cdp-pipe/src/pipe.ts:44, 102-109, 303; docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-06-bridge-b1-design.md:68, 108; docs/ux/scenarios.md:1052, 1057, found by the `product` tier)
